content:
I've so far managed to migrate the noAlphaImports linter to Lean, but I was just wondering how would be best to actually integrate it with all of the other linters.

It's not built as a Batteries.Tactic.Lint linter because (as far as I'm aware) it can't see imports as they're part of the file's header. Instead, the function just returns IO Bool and prints any errors, similar to the existing Python Script.

I just wanted to ask where this should actually be run. I could add it into runPhyslibAlphaLinters or would it be better somewhere else or in an entirely separate build target?

I think the question is:

  • Have you defined it as a linter in the proper Lean sense here?
    If so then runPhyslibAlphaLinters seems appropriate, else a separate build target would work.
No, it's not a linter in the proper sense. I'll make a new build target and then make a PR.

I've now finished converting the second PhyslibAlpha script to Lean (alphaFileImports). I just had a few questions though before I made a PR.
1) I can make some unit tests for this 'linter' (again not a conventional linter), but if that's the case, what would be the best way to go about doing that. I could make a dummy project that violates/passes all rules but this would be quite clunky and could clutter up the repo.
2) The 'linter' checks if PhyslibAlpha.lean imports all files in the PhyslibAlpha/ directory. Would it be useful to extend it to the QuantumInfo and Physlib targets as well?
3) Should I create a separate build target for alphaFileImports, or rename the existing noAlphaImports target to a more general name and move it into there? Should I also include these checks in the lint_all target?

1) I can make some unit tests for this 'linter' (again not a conventional linter), but if that's the case, what would be the best way to go about doing that. I could make a dummy project that violates/passes all rules but this would be quite clunky and could clutter up the repo.

This I don't know the best way of doing it. Maybe we could include files in ./Meta/Test folder which are naively excluded from all linters unless a --test flag is put on them.

2) The 'linter' checks if PhyslibAlpha.lean imports all files in the PhyslibAlpha/ directory. Would it be useful to extend it to the QuantumInfo and Physlib targets as well?

There is already one of these for Physlib and QuantumInfo. Might be useful to combine them. However, the application is different:

  • For PhyslibAlpha, it is ok for the module import to be commented out. In Physlib and QuantumInfo the must be proper imports.

Given this, might be easier to keep them separate.

3) Should I create a separate build target for alphaFileImports, or rename the existing noAlphaImportstarget to a more general name and move it into there? Should I also include these checks in the lint_alltarget?

Yes, including them in lint_all would be nice! If easy, maybe we should put them in the same file with a general name.

Great! I'll put a dummy project in ./Meta/Test and try to add the linters to lint_all.

For the second point though, I didn't realize that commented imports were acceptable. If that's the case, it would be difficult to implement that in Lean and would probably end up just scraping the file itself the same way the current Python script does, so there probably wouldn't be much benefit to moving it to Lean, but if you'd just like to move away from Python I'm happy to try to make it work in Lean anyway.

The benefit from moving away from Python is that it is guaranteed that somebody that is working with Physlib has Lean downloaded with the right version, but it's not guaranteed that they're going to have Python downloaded. It removes a layer of dependencies from the project, having things in Lean rather then having things in Python.
